html:
The Kiowa are a Native American people of the Great Plains, whose language belongs to the Tanoan family, related to that of some Pueblo peoples.

In the 1600s and 1700s they lived in western Montana and the Rocky Mountains, where they became friends of the Crow. They took up the horse and the bison hunt and moved south, reaching the southern Plains by the early 1800s. Around 1790 they made a lasting alliance with the Comanche, and with the Plains Apache who lived alongside them. They raided far into Mexico and Texas.

The Kiowa kept picture calendars that record each summer's Sun Dance and each winter's main event. In 1867 a treaty placed them on a reservation in southwest Oklahoma shared with the Comanche and Apache, the Kiowa-Comanche-Apache lands, and after the Red River War of 1874 and 1875 they were held there for good. Today the Kiowa Tribe is based in Carnegie, Oklahoma, and works to save a language with very few speakers.
sum: The Kiowa are a Native American people of the Great Plains, whose language belongs to the Tanoan family, related to that of some Pueblo peoples.
